name: Oliveira Textiles
old_description: Armed with more than two decades of experience in the textile industry, and motivated by the desire to create more healthful surroundings, I founded Oliveira Textiles in 2007 and introduced 'The Ocean Collection': contemporary coastal patterns printed on hemp and organic cotton. Through extensive research I found that consumers absolutely want to use their purchasing power to support thoughtfully produced goods.  I'm proud to be a part of that shift.
about:
Oliveira Textiles was founded in 2007 in Bristol, Rhode Island, by textile designer Dawn Oliveira. After more than two decades in the textile industry, Oliveira launched the company with a focus on healthful surroundings, introducing "The Ocean Collection" of contemporary coastal patterns printed on hemp and organic cotton.

The studio produces stock fabrics and custom color options, selling fabric by the yard and finished pillows. Printing is done on hemp and organic cotton substrates. The operation runs out of a Bristol studio Byfield Building, and also offers freelance design collaborations and licensing opportunities.

The company serves the home textiles and interior design markets, targeting consumers, designers, and retailers seeking sustainably produced fabrics. Products are shipped worldwide via swatch requests, and the brand extends into design education through the "Design Me A House" podcast co-hosted by Oliveira and architect Katie Hutchison.

Oliveira Textiles was motivated by a desire to create more healthful surroundings and to meet consumer demand for thoughtfully produced goods. The founder emphasizes sustainable materials and contemporary coastal aesthetics as key differentiators.

old_description: Olson’s Sheet Metal Works is Family owned and operated, Established in 1928 by my grandfather, Clifford E. Olson, operated by his son Robert C Olson, and now run by Robert Dale Olson for a third generation, based in Minneapolis Minnesota.
about:
Olson Sheet Metal Works Inc has operated in Minneapolis, Minnesota since 1928. Founded by Clifford E. Olson, the business passed to his son Robert C. Olson and is now led by the third generation, Robert Dale Olson. The company remains family-owned and operated.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication across a range of processes: shearing (up to 10-foot capacity), bending with hand brakes and a 10-foot 300-ton press brake, rolling (sheet, bar, angle, and tube), welding (spot, stick, MIG, TIG), plasma and torch cutting, and polishing. Work is performed in-house from layout through final fabrication.

Projects span architectural and decorative metalwork, including railings, hoods, staircases, custom furniture, doors, gates, copper roofs, planter boxes, hardware, sinks, countertops, backsplashes, display fixtures, fireplace surrounds, and burners. The company works with stainless steel, carbon steel, galvanized, hot-rolled, cold-rolled, copper, aluminum, brass, bronze, gold, silver, lead, and zinc.

The firm emphasizes its multi-generational family ownership and the ability to handle custom jobs in virtually any metal, offering complete layout and fabrication under one roof.

name: Olsun Electrics Corporation
old_description: Nothing less than what you’d expect from Olsun Electrics since 1950
about:
Olsun Electrics Corporation has operated from Richmond, Illinois since 1950, when it was established to serve the electronics industry in the greater Chicago area. The original manufacturing space occupied the back of a downtown Richmond building that housed a dentist office in front, where small thimble transformers were wound for a growing OEM customer base. In 1965, Gus Asta, one of the original partners, purchased the company and expanded the product scope to include power and distribution transformers and reactors.

The company designs and manufactures dry-type transformers from 5 kVA through 5,000 kVA in voltage classes up to 34.5 kV. All production occurs under one roof: design engineering, coil winding (barrel, disc, and block coils with wire and foil), vacuum-pressure impregnation varnish systems, miter and butt-lap core cutting, core-and-coil assembly, sheet-metal enclosure fabrication on CNC shear/punch/form equipment, structural base and clamp fabrication, powder-coat painting, encapsulation with polyester resin and silica sand, bus-bar fabrication in aluminum or copper, and final assembly with interrupter switches and tap changers. A Bystronic 4 kW fiber laser with automated material loading and unloading handles enclosure cutting.

Olsun serves universities and colleges, petrochemical plants, oil-and-gas drilling operations, renewable natural gas facilities, battery energy storage projects, municipal power utilities, marine and ship-to-shore crane installations, architectural glass fabricators, commercial HVAC manufacturers, natural gas power plants, hospitals, hospitality resorts, rail transit, refineries, and OEM brand-label electrical manufacturers—a segment the company has supported continuously since the 1960s.

On October 28, 2019, Olsun earned WBENC National Women's Business Enterprise Certification, confirming at least 51% women ownership and control. The company emphasizes design flexibility for one-of-a-kind transformers alongside standard units, manufactures in the USA, and tests every unit to NEMA ST-20, ANSI C57.12.01, and C57.12.91, with designs meeting NEMA, ANSI, IEEE, IEC, ABS, and DNV requirements.

The company manufactures a range of electrical components including switchgear and transformer components (under the Electromagnetic Industries® brand), custom transformers (Acutran®), T-Bar® switches, fuel pumps, relays, and custom-wound coils.

name: Omni Defense Tech
old_description: Our goal is to enable and enhance mission readiness by offering safe and reliable in-flight relief options for aviators. Omni Defense Technologies designs, develops, and manufactures best-in-class products that support military Aviators on all aircrew ensembles.  Skydrate's Certified Through-Suit Connector maintains environmental seal for Immersion Suits and CBRN Personal Protection Gear, bringing a higher level of performance to the flight deck.
about:
Omni Defense Tech is based in Colchester, Vermont, and was founded on November 20, 1998, by electromechanical engineer Mark Harvie. The company began as a small engineering firm driven by Harvie's passion for aviation and technology.

Today the company designs, develops, and manufactures the SKYDRATE in-flight bladder relief system, including male and female configurations and a certified through-suit connector that maintains environmental seals for immersion suits and CBRN personal protection gear. With eleven U.S. patents, Omni Defense Tech also collaborates with NASA to adapt its waste-management technology for astronaut missions, and its products are deployed worldwide.

The systems serve military aviators across the U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, and partner nations, as well as chem-bio personnel, search-and-rescue teams, and medical professionals. A female F-15E pilot noted the system eliminates the need to unstrap from safety restraints, simplifying cockpit operations.

Harvie founded the company to elevate human performance through safe, non-invasive, hands-off, automatic, and leak-proof relief solutions. The SKYDRATE system passes rigorous USAF and USN flight-safety standards and is marketed as "Certified Safe-To-Fly," reflecting a focus on mission readiness without compromising pilot restraint.

Ontogen Medtech is based in Lisle, Illinois, and began operations in 2021 with a mission to give medical device innovators a strategy-focused, capital-efficient path from concept to commercialization. The company does not publicly disclose its ownership structure or founder names.

Its services span design, prototyping, engineering, testing and validation, regulatory support, and ISO 13485-certified production. Ontogen reports that thousands of devices have been shipped nationwide for its clients, though it does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Clients include early-stage and growth-stage medical device companies such as Flow Medical, Stiehl Tech, Innoblative, and Hubly Surgical. Ontogen's work covers electro-mechanical, reusable, surgical, single-use, and diagnostic devices, and the company highlights its role in helping clients secure grants, patents, and FDA clearances.

Ontogen says its differentiation lies in keeping regulatory strategy, engineering, verification, quality systems, and manufacturing aligned under one roof to eliminate handoff gaps. It emphasizes hands-on execution by senior talent rather than advisory-only engagements, and it focuses on deliverables that de-risk programs—clear requirements, disciplined design controls, and verification plans that withstand scrutiny.

old_description: Custom, distribution, padmount, and PDU transformers (CA plant is secondary to overseas)
about:
Pacific Transformer was founded in 1981 in Anaheim, California, by three softball teammates who each borrowed $1,300 from their parents to start building transformers in a garage. The company remains founder-owned and headquartered in Anaheim, where it operates a domestic production facility alongside international operations in Mexico, Thailand, and China.

The company designs and manufactures custom magnetic components — including transformers (1 VA to 1,000 kVA), toroidals, inductors, chokes, and complete power-solution assemblies — for applications ranging from signal-level toroids to 750 kVA padmount units. Thousands of proven catalog designs are available for immediate shipment, while custom parts are modeled before winding and prototyped in as little as 48 hours. To date, Pacific Transformer has shipped more than 45 million units.

Its customer base spans aerospace (Mars rovers, 400 Hz flight hardware), defense (nuclear submarines, shipboard systems qualified to MIL-PRF-27), medical (low-leakage isolation magnetics for diagnostic imaging), EV infrastructure (Tesla Superchargers), industrial automation, data centers, renewable energy, professional audio, and utilities. Clients include NASA, the Department of Defense, Tesla, General Motors, and Otis Worldwide, as well as startups and regional manufacturers ordering prototype to mid-volume runs.

Pacific Transformer differentiates itself by managing the entire ecosystem around magnetics: affordable world pricing backed by owned overseas facilities with a U.S. failover plant, free engineering design and rapid prototyping with no obligation, quality systems certified to ISO 9001 and AS9100D, deep expertise in agency approvals (UL, CSA, CE, ETL, TÜV), and turnarounds — quotes in 24 hours, prototypes in 48 hours — all supported by an engineering team that stays with the project from concept through production.

name: Palmetto Welding & Fabrication Services, LLC
old_description: Needed a pin and weld and was greeted with the best customer service, Amanda is amazing, and Michael is very knowledgeable. I highly recommend this shop to anyone looking for welding services. Among the rest ! ! !
about:
Palmetto Welding & Fabrication Services, LLC was founded in February 2019 by Amanda Koch and Michael Meyer in Summerville, South Carolina. The husband-and-wife team relocated from Wyoming and Texas in 2018, bringing Michael’s extensive welding background and Amanda’s administrative experience to launch a mobile welding operation that quickly grew into a full-service fabrication and erection company.

The shop specializes in structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication and erection, working with carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum. Capabilities include SMAW, GMAW, FCAW, and GTAW welding in all positions, a plasma burn table that cuts plate up to one inch thick, and production of items such as ladders, handrails, stairs, RTU frames, bollards, and canopies. In January 2020 the company moved into a 9,500-square-foot facility on two acres and employs 17 skilled workers, with plans to expand into a 30,000-square-foot building in early 2022.

Palmetto serves industries including oil and gas, marine, nuclear, automotive, and structural steel construction across the Southeast region. The company’s AISC certification for both fabrication and erection allows it to bid on projects with stringent quality requirements, and its licensed and insured status supports work for commercial and industrial clients.

The business was started after Michael identified a local need for skilled, affordable welding services for both production and mobile work. The founders emphasize adapting to client needs, with Michael’s certifications across all metals and positions and Amanda’s operational management forming the core of their competitive position.

name: Paragon Woodworking
old_description: Paragon is a hybrid spatial consulting and custom fabrication studio, quietly serving Northern Utah's most considered residential addresses. We engineer architectural cabinetry from a single shop floor in Pleasant View, for the architects, designers and homeowners who notice every reveal.
about:
Paragon Woodworking operates from a single shop floor in Pleasant View, Utah, serving nine counties across the Wasatch Front. The studio was founded in 2015 by Jon Anglesey, who brought 35 years of hands-on cabinetmaking experience to the venture. Anglesey remains directly involved in every design and layout that passes through the studio.

The company produces architectural-grade custom cabinetry and millwork for luxury residential interiors, specializing in frameless kitchen construction, bespoke vanities, integrated library systems, entertainment hubs, laundry rooms, and tailored closets. Two product lines share a common platform: the Custom Shop Series offers unrestricted design with shadow-line detailing and integrated LED lighting, while the ECO Line standardizes flat-slab profiles with pre-engineered subcrowns to cut installation time by two-thirds and reduce cost by 25–35%. Construction relies on interlocking blind-dado joinery, glued and screwed at every joint, with 3/4-inch drawer sidewalls, 1/2-inch bottoms, and Salice rack-and-pinion full-extension slides rated 33–50 lbs above competing hardware. Finishes are Italian waterborne urethanes with a proprietary cross-linker, delivering zero-VOC, zero-HAPS surfaces.

Clients include architects, designers, builders, and homeowners across Salt Lake, Davis, Weber, Summit, Cache, Box Elder, Morgan, Utah, and Wasatch counties. Projects range from new custom homes to full remodels, with the studio managing design, engineering, fabrication, and white-glove installation.

Paragon was started to elevate cabinetry from a trade to an architectural discipline, emphasizing total transparency in materials and pricing, continuous technical refinement, environmental stewardship through low-emission materials, and architectural respect for the client's space and investment.

name: Parts Unlimited Interiors, Inc.
old_description: Parts Unlimited Interiors is one of those successful entrepreneurial business stories where one thing has led to another, and the small company continues to expand and grow in a controlled, logical fashion. Literally founded physically in a 1964 Corvair's trunk (so to speak), PUI has expanded to the Morrises' basement, to the Jefferson Trade Center in December of 1984, to a 51,400-square foot facility in Louisville, KY, and currently to a 120,000-square foot facility in Oldham County Business Park, La Grange, KY that houses over 100 employees. Approximately 97% to 98% of Parts Unlimited Interiors products are manufactured in the USA, while eight to nine percent of product sales are attributed to being items manufactured overseas. Having most of the parts produced in the United States and most of the sales attributed to U.S. made parts is a success story in and of itself. But Parts Unlimited Interiors isn't resting on its laurels.
about:
Parts Unlimited Interiors operates from a 120,000-square-foot facility in La Grange, Kentucky, in the Oldham County Business Park. The company traces its origins to 1974, when Rollo Fox and his wife Colleen (née Morris) attended a Corvair collectors' convention in Chicago and sold new-old-stock parts from their car trunk. Colleen's father, H.V. Morris, had recommended the Corvair as economical transportation, and the couple's early success selling surplus parts led them to advertise in enthusiast magazines and eventually reproduce Corvair interior components.

The company manufactures interior soft-trim and hard-goods for classic American vehicles, including seat upholstery, door panels, headliners, window felts, console carpet, and insulation products. Production spans GM (Chevrolet, Pontiac, Buick), Ford, and Mopar models. The La Grange plant houses over 100 employees, with more than 80 automotive interior artisans overseeing computer-controlled machinery. Approximately 97–98% of products are made in the United States, with the remainder sourced overseas.

Parts Unlimited Interiors sells primarily through a network of over 100 aftermarket dealers across the U.S. and internationally, offering wholesale and dealer pricing. Its customer base includes restoration shops, classic-car enthusiasts, and dealers specializing in muscle-car and vintage-vehicle interiors. The product portfolio covers a wide range of GM, Ford, and Mopar applications, from Impalas and Camaros to Mustangs and Chargers.

The business pivoted from reselling finite NOS parts to manufacturing reproductions when original supplies dwindled. After being acquired by Restoration Parts Unlimited in August 2013 and later by Classic Industries in October 2023, the company reports that raw-material lead times dropped from several months to two to three weeks, and dealer delivery lead times fell to under one month. The firm emphasizes its U.S.-based manufacturing, deep artisan expertise, and same-day or next-day shipping on stocked items as key differentiators.

about:
Pascetti Steel Design, Inc. operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company is a family-owned shop founded by Damian Pascetti, who spent his career in steel starting with his father's structural steel business before opening Pascetti Steel Design. Management oversees every project directly, reflecting the small-shop structure.

The firm provides turnkey custom steel fabrication for commercial and residential projects. Its scope runs from design and shop drawings through fabrication, delivery, and installation. Core products include steel stair and railing packages, custom balconies, steel canopies, large-scale architectural light fixtures, perforated metal panels, shade structures, custom gates, signage, and public art. The shop also handles historic restoration metalwork and has developed a patent-pending gym equipment system called the Phat Rack™. Work is designed in CAD and prefabricated for field installation.

Clients span architects, designers, general contractors, and homeowners. Projects have been delivered for commercial buildings, hotels and resorts, fitness facilities, municipal landmarks, and cultural institutions. Notable examples include the USS Albuquerque submarine monument restoration, the Penguin Chill exhibit at the ABQ BioPark, and historic railing restorations in Albuquerque, Durango (CO), and Dayton (OH). The company also supplies pre-finished aluminum balcony railing for hospitality projects.

Pascetti Steel positions itself on personalized service and a willingness to take on complex, one-of-a-kind projects that other fabricators may decline. Its stated mission is to foster strong relationships and deliver quality products as a partner, leveraging cutting-edge technology and a strong work ethic.

about:
Pennsylvania Farm Table Company was founded in 2013 by Bobby Snyder in Exton, Pennsylvania. A third-generation woodworker, Snyder learned the craft from his grandfather, Jack, who built dulcimers and banjos, and his father, who taught him the trade. The company began with a vision of creating high-quality farm tables that would become family heirlooms.

The company handcrafts custom farmhouse dining tables using traditional woodworking techniques, with a specialty in hand-turned legs. All furniture is built from locally sourced, sustainable Pennsylvania hardwoods. Operations take place in a recently expanded custom workshop, and a showroom is housed in the restored 1750 West Whiteland Inn, a historic landmark in Exton. The shop produces both made-to-order tables in custom dimensions, wood species, and styles, as well as a selection of pre-built tables available for immediate purchase.

The primary customers are residential homeowners seeking heirloom-quality dining furniture. Testimonials from clients such as Bonnie K., Tesha Maria P., and Derrick B. describe tables that become the focal point of their homes. The company works closely with each customer through the design process, and its pieces have attracted attention from media outlets and HGTV personality Clint Harp.

Snyder started the business after trying several industries, realizing his calling was to use his woodworking skills to create lasting furniture. The firm emphasizes its multi-generational craft heritage, sustainable local materials, and a commitment to building "modern heirlooms" intended to be cherished for generations. Recognition from national media and design awards underscores the quality of their work.

Piedmont Food Processing Center operates in Hillsborough, North Carolina. Clients range from first‑time entrepreneurs to established professionals producing packaged foods, running catering and meal‑prep operations, or launching food trucks. The center works closely with regulatory bodies including the NCDA, Orange County Health Department, USDA, FDA, OSHA, and the Department of Homeland Security to help clients navigate compliance.

The organization emphasizes a low‑risk entry model: no annual fees or contracts, exclusive kitchen use during reserved blocks, and hands‑on business development support. It also highlights a focus on women food entrepreneurs and a community of approachable expertise that helps clients move from concept to market.

The company works with both domestic and international clients, offering turnkey manufacturing from initial part concept through to finished, packaged products.

The company's stated mission is to be more than a manufacturer by building long-term partnerships through a customer-focused team environment. Plastech emphasizes competitive pricing and quality, leveraging over 20 years of strategic partnerships with three offshore tooling factories to manage tooling costs while keeping production domestic.

name: Port Clinton Manufacturing Co
old_description: More than making individual parts, PCM specializes in mating parts together through various methods including brazing and mechanical fits producing a precision assembly for additional machining or ready for assembly.
about:
Port Clinton Manufacturing Co. was founded in 1929 in Port Clinton, Ohio. The company has remained a closely held family corporation, locally owned and operated as a family business for nearly a century.

The shop specializes in high-value-added hardened, ground, and precision parts, with a focus on precision assemblies that mate components through brazing and mechanical fits. Its 68,000-square-foot facility houses 25 automatic screw machines capable of work up to 3-1/2 inches, supplemented by CNC lathes, CNC and multi-spindle chuckers handling blanks up to 12 inches in diameter, and a broaching department with 12 machines rated to a 54-inch stroke and 15 tons. Secondary machining covers grinding (ID, OD, centerless, double-disk, Blanchard), thread rolling, knurling, drilling, tapping, cross-drilling, deep-hole drilling, countersinking, honing, milling, tumbling, bead blasting, cut-to-length, grooving, slotting, trimming, and chamfering. Heat treating and coatings are managed through a qualified external network, while engineering, estimating, and tooling support are provided in-house.

The company serves diesel-engine applications for railroad, oil-and-gas mining, emergency power generation, and off-highway agricultural and construction equipment, as well as mechanical power transmission components such as mine safety devices, heavy-truck transmissions, and brake systems. It operates as a Tier 1 supplier to major engine manufacturers and counts several Fortune 500 companies among its long-term customers, some for over 50 years.

Port Clinton Manufacturing emphasizes total customer satisfaction and a zero-defect culture, backed by PPAP capability, a full inspection lab (CMM, optical comparator, surface finish, magnaflux, Rockwell hardness, ultrasonic cleaning, and Millipore particle counting), and a Dun & Bradstreet AAA rating. The owners’ personal attention to each account and continuous improvement in manufacturing efficiency are cited as key differentiators.

The company positions itself as a technical partner rather than a pure material supplier, emphasizing its team of materials engineers who average 15-plus years of industry experience. It maintains deep inventory positions to buffer supply disruptions, provides full traceability documentation with every shipment, and holds ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, and ITAR registrations across its quality system.

about:
Portland Garment Factory (PGF) was founded in 2008 in Portland, Oregon, by Britt Howard. The woman-owned studio began as a zero-waste creative design and fabrication shop aiming to upend the traditional factory model through ethical labor practices and environmental sustainability.

The company provides full-service soft-goods manufacturing, including custom cut-and-sew production (20,000+ units), art fabrication, product development, prototyping, and retail/experiential fabrication. Operations run in-house with a team of 11–50 employees, supported by an internal experimentation lab (PGF Lab) for material and process innovation.

PGF serves designers, brands, agencies, and artists across apparel, retail, experiential marketing, art institutions, corporate branding, food and beverage, sports, technology, and hospitality. Clients have included Nike, Adidas, Intel, Portland Art Museum, Tillamook, Xbox, Converse, UGG, and DiGiorno, among others.

The studio’s differentiation rests on its zero-waste commitment, B Corporation certification, WBENC woman-owned certification, and Sustainability at Work Gold certification. Core values—Be Human, Think Forward, Honor Process, Respect Time, Invite Challenge—guide a model that blends creative ideation with responsible production.

about:
Power Engineering & Manufacturing, Ltd. (PEM) was founded in 1975 in Waterloo, Iowa, by Saul Herscovici and several members of the Warren family. The company specializes in the custom design and manufacturing of heavy-duty gearboxes and has operated continuously from its Iowa headquarters for nearly five decades.

PEM provides complete gearbox solutions including design, manufacturing, reverse engineering, rebuild, and inspection services. Its machining capabilities encompass 12 CNC lathes, five CNC milling machines, two Okuma MCR-A5CII double-column machining centers, six CNC hobbing machines, five gear grinding machines, and additional grinding, shaping, keyseating, plasma cutting, sawing, dynamic balancing, robotic welding, and stress-relieving equipment. The facility also houses two large-capacity coordinate measuring machines for inspection.

The company serves customers in defense, aerospace, mining, and general industrial markets. Notable projects include AD-43 gearboxes for the U.S. Navy and units for helicopter test stands and roll crushers. PEM also repairs and rebuilds gearboxes from manufacturers such as Falk, Demag, Flender, and Dodge, and supports clients across the United States and in more than 48 countries.

PEM emphasizes ingenuity, attention to detail, and customer service as differentiators. Its proprietary MEGAGEAR® design can increase horsepower or torque by up to 35% over OEM designs, and the company offers expedited service and storage agreements to minimize downtime. Quality is managed under an ISO 9001:2015 certified system, and welding procedures are qualified to AWS D1.1, D1.5, D1.6, and NAVSEA standards.

about:
Precision Metalworks LLC operates from a shop on Dunbar Street in Fremont, Nebraska. The business was founded in 2019 as a part-time welding venture by a single craftsman working after hours, building a reputation one job at a time. What began with one machine and mobile repairs has grown into a full-time fabrication and welding operation serving eastern Nebraska.

The company provides three core services: mobile welding that brings equipment to farms and plants, repair welding for cracked or worn components, and custom fabrication from prints or rough sketches. In-house capabilities include a MultiCam 3000 waterjet with KMT pump, an Amada shear, an Amada press brake, Syncrowave AC/DC TIG welders, and MIG welding for production steel work. The shop works in stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel ranging from 22-gauge sheet to structural plate, handling everything from sanitary food-grade vessels to heavy equipment buckets and trailer frames.

Customers span food processing plants that require sanitary stainless welds, agricultural operations needing field repairs on combines and tillage tools, trailer owners with hitch and gooseneck damage, and industrial shops requiring brackets, racks, guards, and one-off structural parts. The mobile unit travels daily across eastern Nebraska, covering communities from Omaha to Schuyler.

The founder's intent was to keep work in-house rather than subcontract cutting and forming, shortening lead times and keeping a single point of accountability. The same tolerances demanded by food plants are applied to every trailer hitch and bracket, delivered at small-shop pricing with direct phone access.

about:

The company combines single-use endoscopes with cloud-based software to make minimally invasive visualization more efficient, consistent, and safe. While the founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the board includes representatives from Piney Lake Capital Management and former Medtronic executives.

The company's flagship product, Summit™, is a first-of-its-kind 4K single-use surgical arthroscope delivered through a "Scopes as a Subscription™" model with transparent pricing and automated inventory management. Pristine Surgical is developing a full portfolio of rigid and flexible endoscopes spanning arthroscopy, laparoscopy, and flexible endoscopy, addressing a market of approximately 125 million procedures worldwide each year.

The company serves hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and orthopedic surgeons specializing in sports medicine. Clinical users include Southern California Orthopedic Institute, UCLA, Hospital for Special Surgery in New York, Virtua Health in New Jersey, Doral Surgery Center in Florida, and Stetson Lee Orthopaedics in California. The medical advisory board features prominent orthopedic surgeons such as Mark Getelman, MD, David McAllister, MD, Stephen Snyder, MD, and Riley Williams III, MD.

Pristine Surgical was started to remove inefficiency, variability, and safety issues from the endoscopy suite. Conventional reusable systems require costly maintenance contracts, sterilization services, and repairs, while dirty or damaged scopes disrupt workflow and present safety risks. The single-use platform eliminates cleaning and maintenance, reduces operating room setup and teardown time, and provides a new high-definition image for every procedure.

The company has been locally owned and operated since its inception, founded on the principle that strong customer relationships are built through high-quality services at fair prices, with an emphasis on integrity and transparency.

Its service portfolio spans high-, medium-, and low-voltage power distribution, including pole setting, overhead line work, switchgear and transformer installation, motor control center (MCC) and variable frequency drive (VFD) installation and commissioning. In-house capabilities extend to electrical design using AutoCAD Electrical, PLC and SCADA system design, programming, and upgrades, HMI programming, instrument installation and calibration, and industrial communications such as fiber and copper Ethernet and network configuration.

P-I-E serves industrial clients across sectors that require electrical infrastructure, control systems, and automation solutions, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named customers.

P-I-E was founded on the principle that strong customer relationships are formed by offering high-quality services at fair prices, emphasizing integrity and transparency. old_description: Same products. Same solutions. Now backed by the speed of Forgent.
about:
PwrQ operates from Hanover, Maryland, tracing its roots to 1926. The company is now a subsidiary of Forgent, which brought together over a century of power‑systems experience to address modern infrastructure challenges. No individual founders are named in the available sources.

The firm designs and manufactures low‑voltage power distribution equipment — including S1 switchboards, remote power panels (RPP), panelboards, power distribution units (PDU), and automatic transfer switches — through vertically integrated facilities that handle copper busbar fabrication, CNC turret punching, laser cutting, robotic welding, and final assembly and test. Dedicated production lanes for each product family enable high‑volume, high‑precision output. In‑house electrical and application engineering teams perform power‑systems engineering, reliability studies, short‑circuit coordination, arc‑flash analysis, and SCADA/BMS integration. Field services cover preventive maintenance, inspection and testing of medium‑ and low‑voltage switchgear, breakers, relays, and transformers, as well as generator solutions ranging from 3 kW to 10 MW with paralleling and microgrid controls.

PwrQ serves hyperscale data centers, manufacturing plants, utility grids, hospital campuses, and other mission‑critical industrial facilities where uptime and scalability are essential. Its engineering approach spans the full single‑line diagram from utility entrance to rack‑level load, and its service teams are strategically positioned for national and global response.

The company emphasizes that vertical integration gives it control over product development, quality, lead times, and capacity; dedicated lanes and AI‑driven machinery ensure consistency at speed; and its combined product, engineering, and field‑service portfolio allows end‑to‑end delivery without reliance on third‑party vendors.

name: Pyramid Semiconductor
old_description: Pyramid Semiconductor is a manufacturer of semiconductor Integrated Circuits including MIL-STD-1750A Processors, SRAMs, EEPROMs and FCT/FCT-T Logic.
about:
Pyramid Semiconductor is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California. The company was formed in January 2003 through the acquisition of all product lines from Performance Semiconductor, continuing support for all previously supported parts under the same part numbering scheme. On March 8, 2021, HEICO Corporation's Electronic Technologies Group acquired Pyramid Semiconductor LLC, and the business now operates as part of HEICO/3D PLUS USA in the Silicon Valley area.

As a fabless semiconductor manufacturer, Pyramid designs and supplies integrated circuits including MIL-STD-1750A processors, SRAMs, EEPROMs, FCT/FCT-T logic, and flash memory. Wafers are fabricated at outside foundries—TSMC in Taiwan and LA Semiconductor in the USA—while the company's 10,000-square-foot facility handles wafer testing, ceramic and plastic assembly, environmental testing, electrical testing, burn-in, marking, and quality assurance. The site includes a Class 1000 clean room for hermetic ceramic assembly and supports more than 100 Standard Military Drawings (SMDs). Pyramid also offers custom logic functions, packages, and multi-chip modules with short lead times.

The company serves military, aerospace, industrial, and commercial customers, with a focus on high-longevity applications for legacy military embedded systems. Its products are used in defense and aerospace programs requiring MIL-STD-883 compliance and DLA-qualified manufacturing. Pyramid is the sole source for MIL-STD-1750A processors, which have been field-proven for over 20 years.

Pyramid emphasizes quality as the foundation of customer trust, maintaining ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certifications, a QML-certified manufacturing line per MIL-PRF-38535 Class Q, and laboratory suitability for MIL-STD-883. The company highlights its secure, long-term supply chain, radiation-hardened silicon-on-sapphire devices rated beyond 100 krad, and EEPROMs with greater than 10-year data retention and 100,000-cycle endurance.

old_description: Tens of thousands of SCDUSA and SCD detectors and infrared imaging solutions are manufactured for deployment in demanding applications for defense customers, especially in the Air, Land, Sea, Missile, Security and Surveillance domains, where environmental qualification is required.
about:
Quantum Imaging operates as SCD USA Infrared LLC from Colorado Springs, Colorado, with a second site in Melbourne, Florida. The business was established as a fully owned U.S. subsidiary of Israel-based Semiconductor Devices (SCD), a company with more than 40 years of experience in infrared detector development. No founding year for the U.S. entity is publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures infrared detectors and integrated imaging solutions spanning the short-wave (SWIR), mid-wave (MWIR), and long-wave (LWIR) bands. Its product line includes camera cores, engines, and Integrated Detector Dewar Cooler Assemblies (IDDCA) built on semiconductor materials such as InSb, XBn, InGaAs, Type II Superlattice (T2SL), and Vanadium Oxide (VOx). The firm emphasizes its Very Large-Scale Integrated Circuit (VLSI) design capability for readout circuits and says it has delivered tens of thousands of detectors for fielded systems.

Primary customers operate in defense and homeland security — air, land, sea, missile, and surveillance domains — with named programs at Raytheon. The portfolio also serves security and surveillance markets (border, airborne, critical infrastructure, coastal, perimeter), commercial sectors (aviation, gas sensing, non-destructive testing, semiconductor inspection, process monitoring), and space applications. Applications range from missile warning systems and driver vision enhancement to furnace temperature mapping and hyperspectral imaging.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative, field-ready, intelligent imaging and detection systems for real-time visualization of mission-critical intelligence in all theaters and environments. It differentiates itself through what it calls the industry's broadest product offering, scalable engine and camera architectures, and material expertise covering the full infrared spectrum from NIR through LWIR.

Quirk Wire Co. Inc. is based in West Brookfield, Massachusetts. The company became 100% employee‑owned in 2007 through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP).

Quirk Wire serves manufacturers of transducers, medical devices, and vibration test equipment, as well as military, instrumentation, temperature‑sensing, wire‑harness assembly, process‑heating, and control applications.

R&D Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1968 in Brownsboro, Alabama, as a supplier of electronic assemblies to the Department of Defense and its prime contractors for military applications.

name: Rail Yard Studios - Custom Furniture Designers and Builders
old_description: Industrial designer and entrepreneur, Robert Hendrick, founded Rail Yard Studios. He designs the company's furniture collections and is in collaboration with other artists, designers, and architects. He began the effort out of a need to round out the cyclical nature of the railroad contracting business he owned.
about:
Rail Yard Studios operates from Nashville, Tennessee. The company was founded by industrial designer and entrepreneur Robert Hendrick, who also owned a railroad contracting business. He started the furniture venture to complement the cyclical nature of that business. Ownership is shared among Hendrick, Rob Humphreys, Rick Turner (who joined in 2012), and Jim "Pop" Hendrick.

The studio designs and builds custom furniture using reclaimed steel sourced from railroad renovation projects and natural wood. Their product line includes tables, desks, beds, coffee tables, side tables, poker tables, and custom wine cellars for both residential and commercial spaces. They have developed unique methods of historic preservation that reflect a commitment to sustainability and quality. The workshop is led by production manager and master craftsman Ryan Galbreath, who oversees daily operations, pioneers new material techniques, maintains equipment, and emphasizes safety and a reduced environmental footprint.

The company serves homeowners, offices, interior designers, and architects. Concrete examples include custom conference rooms, statement coffee tables, and bespoke wine cellars. Rail Yard Studios collaborates with artists, designers, and architects to realize client visions.

The founders say the business was driven by a personal commitment to sustainability and quality, developing proprietary historic preservation methods to repurpose authentic railroad materials. They take pride in craftsmanship, passing each piece from their hands to the customer.

about:
Randy's Booth Co. Inc. operates from a renovated facility in Crystal, Minnesota, a northwest suburb of Minneapolis. The business traces its roots to the 1970s when Randy Kissoondath, an immigrant from Trinidad and Tobago, began building restaurant booths and earned a national reputation for custom seating. After a health-related sale and a later restart, Randy's son Bert Kissoondath joined the company in his mid-20s, learning every aspect of production before assuming leadership following his father's sudden death in 2009. The firm relocated to its current 2-acre site in September 2017, gaining 20-foot ceiling clearance, a loading dock, and a showroom.

The company manufactures custom hospitality furnishings—booths, banquettes, chairs, stools, tables, and headboards—using Northern Hardwoods such as cherry, ash, oak, and maple. A 20-person team handles design, fabrication, finishing, and installation in-house, allowing the shop to control quality from raw lumber to final placement. While the earlier iteration employed 40 people serving chains like Hyatt and Perkins, the current operation focuses on a close-knit crew that manages projects from concept through installation.

Customers include restaurant groups, designers, architects, and healthcare and corporate clients across the United States. Recent projects range from multi-unit restaurant build-outs for operators such as Nova Restaurant Group (Hazelwood Food & Drink) and independent owners (Stanley's NE, Pub 819, The Howe Daily Kitchen and Bar) to the Super Bowl celebration at the Minneapolis Armory, where the shop delivered custom walls, poster panels, tables, and seating on a tight timeline.

The company emphasizes generational craftsmanship and a "customized craft in a cut-and-paste world" philosophy. Bert Kissoondath cites his father's lesson that pride in work shows in the finished product, a principle that earned the firm the 2024 Minnesota Manufacturer of the Year award and the SBA's Minnesota Family Owned Business of the Year honor. The leadership team highlights on-time delivery, value engineering, and direct oversight of every installation as key differentiators.

name: Red Cloud Renewable Energy Center
old_description: Native students receive free training that opens the door to a lifelong solar career, every class installs panels for families who need it most, and each kilowatt of solar installed prevents roughly 1.5 tons of CO₂ every year.
about:
Based in Pine Ridge, South Dakota, Red Cloud Renewable Energy Center operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to advancing energy sovereignty in Native American communities. The organization’s founding date and original founders are not publicly disclosed, but its mission centers on providing free, hands-on training in solar installation, weatherization, and sustainable building practices.

The center’s core activity is a workforce development program that combines classroom instruction with field work: each training cohort installs photovoltaic systems on homes of families identified as needing assistance most. This dual approach builds technical skills while delivering immediate energy cost reductions. The curriculum covers photovoltaic system design, safety protocols, and weatherization techniques aimed at improving home resilience in harsh climates. No facility size, headcount, or annual installation volume is published.

Red Cloud Renewable serves Native American students seeking careers in the green energy sector, as well as low-income households on reservations who receive the installed systems. Its work aligns with the broader renewable energy and weatherization industries, and the organization explicitly frames its impact under the banner of 'Support Energy Sovereignty.' Testimonials from program graduates highlight career placement and personal empowerment.

The organization states that its model is a 'new way to honor the old ways,' linking cultural values with modern sustainability. By offering training at no cost and coupling it with direct community installations, it aims to foster self-sufficiency, lower energy bills, and reduce carbon emissions—each kilowatt installed is said to prevent roughly 1.5 tons of CO2 annually.

Custom garments are offered with very low minimum order quantities, either under the Reed brand or as private label.

Reed serves wholesale distributors and direct industrial customers in food processing, general industrial safety, and sectors requiring flame‑resistant or high‑visibility apparel such as oil and gas, utilities, and construction. Its catalog includes dozens of SKUs for FR garments, food‑service coats, and enhanced‑visibility shirts, all sold through a distributor network.

The company emphasizes its long‑standing commitment to “integrity in every stitch,” citing fair pricing, timely delivery, and product durability as core values. Its inventory‑management program is presented as a unique differentiator that helps customers reduce carrying costs, freight expenses, and order‑processing labor.

Renaissance Design Group operates from St. Cloud, Minnesota, where craftsman Mike Fanslau launched the operation in 2018 with the purchase of a Timberking portable sawmill. The company transforms salvaged logs into custom furniture, small structures, and architectural lumber. Services include on-site sawmilling up to 36 inches in diameter, drying in an indoor dehumidification kiln (nine-foot capacity) and a solar kiln (14-foot slabs), and planing up to 25 inches wide and 12 feet long. Fanslau builds he-sheds, she-sheds, outhouses, pet shelters, benches, and a range of epoxy-finished pieces such as coffee tables, mantels, bar tops, and memory tables. The shop also offers epoxy mentorship and a la carte milling services for DIY customers.

Customers include homeowners preserving sentimental trees, residential builders sourcing lumber from lot clearing, and commercial projects seeking Carbon Smart Wood—architectural-grade material from urban salvage. The company picks up downed logs with a hoisted trailer and maintains a rotating inventory of Minnesota hardwoods (oak, ash, maple, walnut, cherry) and softwoods (pine, spruce, fir, tamarack).

Fanslau emphasizes the reuse of meaningful timber, offering coaching on epoxy application and flexible service tiers that let clients participate in the build. The operation partners with larger mills for logs exceeding its capacity, ensuring a single point of contact for the customer.

name: Revolution Bag
old_description: Delta Plastics of the South is founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas, with a focus on providing efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South, and soon after starts recycling to show the importance of being part of the solution to plastic waste.
about:
Revolution Bag, operating as Revolution Company, traces its roots to 1996 when Delta Plastics of the South was founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas. The company began by supplying efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South region and quickly added recycling operations to address plastic waste. In 2008 the business expanded to Little Rock, where it established its first sustainable-loop recycling facility and launched the Revolution Bag line of trash can liners made with up to 97% certified post-consumer resin. The headquarters remain in Little Rock, Arkansas.

Today Revolution manufactures a range of plastic products including trash can liners, carryout bags for foodservice and retail, agricultural films, commercial sheeting, and stretch films. The company runs an integrated circular model: a specialized fleet collects used film, which is cleaned and mechanically recycled at its facilities to produce certified post-consumer and post-industrial resins. Those resins feed both Revolution’s own product lines and the supply chains of global brands and OEMs. The company reports processing more than 300 million pounds of material annually and has diverted over 3 billion pounds from landfills since inception. Growth has come through acquisitions such as Rodeo Plastic Bag & Film, Command Packaging, Encore Recycling, Pak-Sher, Polar Plastics, Jadcore, and Five Point Films, adding capacity in commercial films, consumer bags, post-industrial recycling, and stretch films.

Revolution serves agriculture, food service, construction and commercial supply, consumer goods, restaurants, delis, and grocery chains. Its recycled resins are sold to brands and original equipment manufacturers seeking circular content. A noted reference comes from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, where a sustainability manager reported reducing virgin resin use from hundreds of thousands of pounds to 17,000 pounds annually through Revolution’s programs.

The company was started to demonstrate that plastic can be a valuable resource with infinite usefulness if reclaimed responsibly. Its stated differentiator is a closed-loop business model that controls the entire lifecycle — from collection and recycling to resin production and finished goods — enabling customers to meet ESG goals while maintaining product performance.

Today, the company is led by their son, Paul Spalitta, representing second-generation ownership with a third generation emerging.

The company functions as a broadline distributor, supplying a wide range of food and non-food items including produce, meats, breads, condiments, equipment, smallwares, paper goods, and cleaning supplies. Its distribution facility is located near the I-55/I-12 corridor, enabling rapid delivery across southeast Louisiana and the Mississippi Gulf Coast. S&W serves a diverse customer base of independent and chain restaurants, including donut shops, coffee shops, Tex-Mex, Italian, Mediterranean, family dining, sandwich shops, and seafood establishments. The company emphasizes personal relationships and quick response times, noting it remained operational and made deliveries the day after Hurricanes Ida and Katrina when other distributors could not.

The company's guiding principle, coined by the founder, is "Large enough to serve, small enough to care." S&W differentiates itself through independent ownership that allows flexibility without corporate red tape, a commitment to knowing customers by name, and specialized programs such as custom-cut steaks, fresh produce sourcing through Fresh Concepts, and artisanal cheeses via The Rind Cheese Company.

Management cites 100% U.S. manufacturing, ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, and ISO 13485 certifications, engineering and design competence, flexible supply-chain management, and on-time delivery as the pillars of its "Sag Harbor Advantage."

about:
Selby Electric operates from Mandan, North Dakota, serving Bismarck, Mandan, and the surrounding Burleigh and Morton counties. The business was established by Craig Selby, a North Dakota Master Electrician (license #M4002), who has accumulated over 30 years of hands-on experience in residential and commercial electrical work. Selby runs the company as a sole proprietorship, handling every job personally without subcontractors.

The company provides a full range of electrical services, including recessed lighting installation, ceiling fan wiring and replacement, electrical panel upgrades to meet current code, preventive maintenance inspections, wiring and repair for outlets and full rewires, shop wiring for 240‑volt outlets and sub‑panels, troubleshooting of tripping breakers and flickering lights, electrical work for room additions and remodel projects, and code‑compliant EV charger installations. All work is performed by Selby himself, ensuring consistent quality and direct communication.

Selby Electric serves both residential homeowners and commercial clients across the Bismarck‑Mandan area. Commercial projects have included wiring for shops, offices, and other local businesses, with Selby present on each job site to coordinate with contractors and keep projects on schedule.

Selby emphasizes that his local ownership means he is invested in the community and builds long‑term relationships with customers who rely on him to keep their homes and businesses safe. His differentiators are direct owner involvement on every project, clear communication, and a commitment to completing work correctly the first time.
